chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who made it a thanksgiving to God for a trial with which he was tested, that if God healed him, he would perform the Hajj from al-Kufa. He said, 'Let him perform the Hajj from al-Kufa.'

key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Al-Kufa (a city in Iraq, often used as a Miqat for residents)
key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: To enter the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a vow to perform Hajj as thanks for healing from illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of literal fulfillment in vows (*nadhr*), where the Imam affirms that specifying a location for the start of Ihram binds the vow to that specific act. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on adhering strictly to the vow's wording unless ambiguity exists, distinguishing between the obligation of the ritual act and the geographical origin. This ruling underscores the importance of intention and precise language in personal devotional commitments within Shia fiqh.
